query: What effect do GLP-1 receptor agonists have on IL-6 levels in neuroinflammation studies?
reference_answer: GLP-1 receptor agonists have been shown to significantly reduce IL-6 levels in patients with neuroinflammatory conditions, with reductions of 30-40% reported in randomised controlled trials.

query: Do all studies agree on the efficacy of CRISPR base editing for treating sickle cell disease?
reference_answer: No. While several studies report high efficacy of CRISPR base editing in reactivating fetal haemoglobin, at least one study raises concerns about off-target edits at non-intended genomic sites, suggesting efficacy and safety findings are not yet fully consistent across the literature.

query: What is the proposed mechanism by which the gut microbiome influences anxiety?
reference_answer: The gut-brain axis is implicated via vagal nerve signalling, microbial production of short-chain fatty acids, and modulation of serotonin precursors. Dysbiosis has been associated with altered HPA axis activity and increased anxiety-like behaviour in animal models.

query: What sample sizes are typical in RCTs studying GLP-1 agonists and neuroinflammation?
reference_answer: Sample sizes in this area typically range from 80 to 200 participants, with follow-up periods of 12 to 24 weeks.

query: What biomarkers are most commonly used to measure neuroinflammation in clinical studies?
reference_answer: IL-6, TNF-alpha, and C-reactive protein (CRP) are the most frequently reported biomarkers. Some studies also use neurofilament light chain (NfL) as a marker of neuronal damage.
